source.title: Controlling cell adhesion and degradation of chitosan films by N-acetylation

formulation.evidence: Chitosan films with DAs of 0.5% and 10.9% were synthesized by pouring a 3% (w/w) solution of chitosan of the desired DA in 2% aqueous acetic acid into Petri dishes
Chitosan films with DAs of 0.5% and 10.9% were synthesized by pouring a 3% (w/w) solution of chitosan of the desired DA in 2% aqueous acetic acid into Petri dishes

processing.evidence: Chitosan with a DA of 0.5% was synthesized by immersing commercially available 10.9% acetylated chitosan flakes in a 40% aqueous solution of sodium hydroxide for 2 h at 110 1C.
Films prepared as described in Section 2.2 were sterilized by autoclaving (120 1C, 20 min)

biology.cell_type: primary chick dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons (E9)

culture_days.evidence: Primary chick DRG neurons were cultured for 2 days on films of chitosan and N-acetylated chitosan

other_outcomes.evidence: For chitosan with a DA of 0.5%, cell viability was higher than that on all other materials. Remarkably, it was about 8 times higher than that on chitosan with a DA of 10.9%.
other_outcomes.name: cell viability (MTS) relative to DA 10.9% chitosan

notes: Degradation in PBS pH 7.4, 37 °C with 1.5 mg/ml lysozyme was minimal over 4 weeks; no significant enzymatic degradation.
